User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the DesignDock application, storing their profile information and serving as a link to an external authentication system like Firebase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity. This ID typically corresponds to the user's ID from an external authentication system (e.g., Firebase Auth UID).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

DesignProject.title: DesignProject
DesignProject.description: Represents a design project created and managed by a user in the DesignDock application, including details, links, and associated images.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DesignProject entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this design project. (Relationship: User 1:N DesignProject)

name.description: The name of the design project.

description.description: A detailed description of the design project.

projectName.description: The name of the parent project this design belongs to, used for grouping.

version.description: The version of the design project, e.g., '1.0'.

figmaLink.description: URL to the Figma design file for this project.

prototypeUrl.description: URL to the live prototype of the design project.

imageUrl.description: URL to the associated image (e.g., a thumbnail or full-size project screenshot) for the design project.

tags.description: A list of keywords or tags associated with the design project, potentially generated by an AI tool for better searchability and categorization.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the design project was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the design project was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID '{userId}' must match the Firebase Authentication UID for the user. Includes denormalized 'id' field for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user.

definition.description: Stores design projects, nested under the owning user. The document ID '{designProjectId}' uniquely identifies a project for that user. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence and simplified security rules.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user who owns the project.

params.name: designProjectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the design project.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for DesignDock prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles, particularly Authorization Independence and QAPs. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
This is achieved primarily through a hierarchical data structure combined with explicit ownership fields. 
1.  **User Profiles:** Each user's profile is stored at `/users/{userId}`. The document ID (`{userId}`) directly corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID (`request.auth.uid`). This means that a user's profile can be accessed without needing to perform a `get()` operation on a separate document to verify ownership. The `id` field within the User document itself will match the document ID, reinforcing this.
2.  **Design Projects:** Design projects are stored in a subcollection under the owning user: `/users/{userId}/designProjects/{designProjectId}`. The `DesignProject` document itself also contains a `userId` field. This denormalization is crucial: while the path already indicates ownership, explicitly storing `userId` within *every* `DesignProject` document ensures that authorization rules can be evaluated based solely on the `request.auth.uid` and the document's own fields (`resource.data.userId`), without requiring any `get()` calls to the parent `/users/{userId}` document. This allows for atomic operations (e.g., creating a new user and their first project in a batch) and makes security rules simple and robust (e.g., `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId;`).

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structure supports secure `list` operations by implementing **Structural Segregation** (Mandate B).
1.  **User Profiles:** The `/users/{userId}` collection ensures that an authenticated user can only `get` or `list` their own user document, as the document ID directly matches their `uid`. Any attempt to list all users without proper admin privileges would be blocked by rules.
2.  **Design Projects:** By nesting design projects under the user's path (`/users/{userId}/designProjects`), any `list` operation on this subcollection (`db.collection('users').doc(userId).collection('designProjects').get()`) will inherently only retrieve projects belonging to the specific `{userId}` in the path. Combined with security rules that verify `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path wildcard) and `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` (from the denormalized field), the system guarantees that users can only list their *own* projects. This eliminates the need for `where` clauses in security rules, as the structure itself enforces the necessary access control for `list` operations, preventing unauthorized data from ever being returned.

This design ensures that authorization logic is clear, easy to debug, and maintains performance by avoiding costly `get()` operations in rules and leveraging Firestore's native hierarchical security model.
